Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Australia's reply. The umpires and the players of England are back out in the middle. It will be the dup of Travis Head and Jake Weatherald to open the innings for Australia. Brydon Carse will start proceedings with the ball and there's a leg slip in place as well for Head right away. Let's play...
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Australia will feel they have done extremely well to keep England down to 384 here but 384 is still a big number if we are to go about the scores in this series. Also, the ball is doing a bit off the deck and the bounce has been uneven, especially in the last few overs, which will make the job of the Aussie openers all the more difficult and crucial as well. It should be a cracking last session of play, so stick around.

Play resumed after Lunch with England 336/6 in 78 overs and after a couple of overs from the part-timers, Australia switched to Mitchell Starc and Scott Boland. Joe Root remained largely unfazed and Will Jacks too did well to not get out against the extra seam movement and bounce. The duo stitched together a 50-run stand but once the two danger bowlers were taken off the attack, Jacks threw away all the hard work. Root went on to surpass 150 but Neser bowled a lovely spell and picked up 3 out of the remaining 4 wickets, including that of Root for 160.

SESSION SUMMARY - 19.3 overs, 48 runs and 4 wickets. With the end of England's first innings and 20 minutes or so left for the actual Tea break, the umpires decide to take early Tea. For the first hour, it seemed like England's session but the likes of Michael Neser and Cameron Green have come in and get rid of the English tail in a jiffy.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to the post-Lunch session on Day 2. The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the Aussie players. Joe Root is all set to resume his stay at the crease alongside Will Jacks. Just a couple of overs left before the 2nd new ball is available and it will be Marnus Labuschagne to start proceedings with the ball after the break. Let's go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Australia’s bowling unit was largely superb, reaping the rewards of tighter, more disciplined lines compared to the previous day. The seam attack, spearheaded by excellent opening spells from Boland and Starc, troubled the batters consistently and was ably supported by Michael Neser and Cameron Green. However, just as the partnership between Joe Root and Jamie Smith began to look formidable, Marnus Labuschagne was introduced into the attack just before the break and provided a crucial intervention. He broke the troublesome stand, dismissing Smith for 46, a vital breakthrough that gave his side a much-needed boost heading into the Lunch interval. The contest remains finely poised as the players head for Lunch, with Root, England's lynchpin, now needing to rebuild again during the post-Lunch session. We will be back by 2.10 am GMT.

The dismissal of Brook initiated a brief flurry of activity. England's captain, Ben Stokes, arrived at the crease intending to play the long game but departed almost immediately, registering a duck as Mitchell Starc produced a beauty that, bolstered by a sharp review from Steve Smith, dismissed the England captain. The situation appeared precarious for England at 229/5, but the arrival of Jamie Smith brought a different dynamic. Smith rode his luck, notably surviving a scare when caught off Cameron Green's no-ball on 22, and partnered resiliently with Root to forge a vital 94-run stand for the sixth wicket.

LUNCH, DAY 2. Australia have put in a much better performance in a compelling morning session at the SCG, following a difficult Day 1, and restricted England from running away with the contest by making crucial breakthroughs before the Lunch interval. Resuming at an overnight score of 211/3, the English batters added 125 runs in 33 overs but rarely found their rhythm, operating under constant pressure from a disciplined Australian attack. The early tentative boundary proved a shadow for the session's narrative, a consistent battle for survival rather than assertion. The overnight pair of Joe Root and Harry Brook struggled to build significantly on their partnership before Scott Boland made the decisive incision, removing the dangerous Brook for a well-made 84 and triggering a shift in momentum.

What were you doing, Mr. Root? A reverse sweep just at the stroke of Lunch and he gets lucky that the ball comes off his glove and bounces onto the deck before Alex Carey gathers this behind the stumps. Commentary.Commentary: Australia on the other hand will be eager for early wickets on Day 2 as they know if they allow this pair to settle in, it could be a long day in the field. So far in this series, we have seen numerous collapses with the bat and both teams, especially England have thrown it away when in a position of promise. Will that trend continue in Sydney as well? We shall find out. Stay tuned as live action isn't far away now.

Day 1 of the 'Pink Ashes Test' saw England have a solid day out with the bat and after a period where they seemed to be crumbling quickly, the duo of Joe Root and Harry Brook has taken them into a commanding position with the bat. Both Root and Brook will be looking to navigate through the first half an hour or so and then look for their individual centuries.

Hello and welcome back to the iconic Sydney Cricket Ground for Day 2 of the 5th and final Ashes Test match. After the inclement weather on the afternoon of Day1, we now head into a new day and thankfully, things are looking much brighter and we should get a full day's worth of play in.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Ultimately, the day concluded prematurely as the final session was entirely washed out by a combination of deteriorating light and rain. Play was officially abandoned, leaving England in a commanding position. The visitors will be thrilled with their substantial total and strong partnership, while Australia faces the daunting task of breaking the formidable Root-Brook stand when play resumes tomorrow, weather permitting. We are in for an early start as well to cover the loss of overs. The first ball will be bowled at 11 pm GMT (On Sunday), but you can join us in advance for the build-up as well. Cheers!

The afternoon session further solidified England's control, with Root and Brook completely neutralizing the Australian threat. They notched up their respective fifties and built an unbroken 154-run partnership. The Australian bowlers toiled for 21 fruitless overs in the post-Lunch session, creating only half-chances as England added a commanding 97 runs without losing a wicket before bad light forced an early tea break.

Following the flurry of wickets, the experienced Joe Root and Harry Brook expertly navigated the testing Australian attack. The pair showcased exceptional composure to guide England safely to the Lunch interval, adding a crucial 57 runs at a healthy clip. At that point, Root was unbeaten on 31 and Brook on 23, both well-set to build on their promising start. While Starc, Boland, and Michael Neser each claimed a wicket, the home side's bowling unit largely struggled to contain the flow of runs.

STUMPS, DAY 1 - We have had a curtailed day but England have done pretty well on the opening day of the fifth and final Ashes Test in Sydney, seizing the initiative after winning the toss and electing to bat on a pitch that offered minimal assistance to the Australian bowlers despite a good grass covering. Openers Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett established a confident foundation, with Duckett in particular showing aggressive intent early on. However, Australia found brief joy when Mitchell Starc dismissed Duckett yet again. Jacob Bethell couldn't do much with the bat and perished on 10 as well.

UPDATE - 6.03 am GMT - The umpires are heading towards the dressing room. There it is, we have the dreaded news and PLAY HAS BEEN CALLED OFF ON DAY 1. Also, it seems like there will be an early start on Monday, at 11 pm GMT ( the previous day).

Things have not gone very dark but the storm seems to have picked up as well and according to a few sources, a few umbrellas are flying away as well. Unfortunately, things do not look any more optimistic right now. Actually, scratch that previous update and it is getting brighter at the SCG. You just can't catch a break with this type of weather lets hope that it continues to brighten up. Stay tuned for more updates.

Resumption now hinges on a demanding sequence of requirements - first, the rain must cease entirely, second, the ground staff must restore the playing surface to a safe condition, and finally, natural light levels must improve to meet the established benchmark. With these multiple obstacles to clear, the prospects of play resuming in the immediate future appear increasingly slim.

UPDATE - 4.53 am GMT - More bad news, folks! It has started to rain now here in Sydney. However, it is not that heavy, and hopefully it is just a passing shower. The drainage here is one of the best in the world, and it wouldn't take long to prepare the ground once the rain stops. Stick with us for more news.

UPDATE - 4.30 am GMT - The start of the final session on Day 1 has been delayed as visibility at the SCG continues to deteriorate. While the anticipated storm has yet to break, an ominous gloom has settled over the ground, leaving on-field umpires with no choice but to keep the players in the pavilion for safety. With heavy thunderstorms and darkening skies forecasted for the remainder of the evening, a resumption of play looks increasingly unlikely.
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

The pair of Joe Root and Harry Brook has been unbreakable for Australia, who toiled hard for 21 overs in this session and managed to create only a couple of half-chances, that too because of Brook's overeagerness, nothing more than that. The duo notched up their respective fifties, much to the delight of the Barmy Army, and their partnership is now worth 154 runs, the third-highest fourth-wicket stand for England in the Ashes. They will look to carry on in the same vein when they return, while the Aussies will be desperate to break this partnership before the end of the day’s play. Hopefully, in about 20 minutes, it all gets cleared up, and we get into the final session. We will be back by 4.10 am GMT.

With only around 10 minutes to go until the scheduled Tea, the umpires have decided to take EARLY TEA, which makes complete sense in the circumstances. So, what happened in this session? Well, it was dominated by England as they managed to go through without losing any wickets, and added 97 runs to the total as well. They would not have wanted to go off, but the Aussies actually would not mind this and can take this opportunity to come up with some new plans and tactics to get back in the game.

UPDATE - 3.56 am GMT - As dark clouds loomed and visibility diminished, the on-field umpires utilized the light meter during the over change to determine that conditions had become insufficient for safe play. By halting the match at this juncture, the specific reading recorded now serves as the official benchmark for the remainder of the game. Consequently, play can only resume if light levels improve beyond this threshold.

By the end of the morning session, the pair had added a vital 57 runs off just 66 balls, setting the stage for a potentially big first-inning total. Root is unbeaten on 31, and Brook stands tall on 23, both looking set to play the long game. The Australian bowlers, while decent, struggled to contain the flow of runs, though Starc, Boland, and Michael Neser each managed to pick up a wicket. Cameron Green, who bowled four overs, remains wicketless so far as England ended the session in a strong position. We will be back with the post-Lunch session around 2.10 am GMT.

The flow of wickets briefly shifted momentum, but Zak Crawley continued to hold his ground, though he was unlucky to be given out on the Umpire's call after being trapped on the front foot. Following his dismissal, the experienced Joe Root and the in-form Harry Brook navigated the challenging Australian bowling attack adeptly. The duo displayed excellent composure to see out the remainder of the session, scoring at a decent pace and building a crucial partnership for England.

LUNCH, DAY 1 - England have started the final Test of the Ashes series, the Pink Test, on a solid footing after winning the toss and electing to bat first on a pitch with a tinge of grass that has offered no demons so far. Openers Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett began confidently, with Duckett in particular starting on the front foot and looking to assert early dominance. Despite Duckett's aggressive intent, which saw him hit two consecutive boundaries, his positive start was cut short when he fell to a sharp delivery from Mitchell Starc. This brought Jacob Bethell to the crease, who, unfortunately for the visitors, didn't last long, as a brilliant outgoing delivery from Scott Boland found his outside edge, neatly taken by Alex Carey behind the stumps.
Fuller one and on middle, angling in, Harry Brook clips it away with nice timing to the right of mid on and gets three runs. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: All set to begin the final Test of the Ashes 2025/26! It is a packed-out SCG as expected, and the Barmy Army are also in full voice. Now, the Australian players make their way out to the middle and spread out to take their respective field positions. Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett are the two openers for England. Mitchell Starc has the new red cherry in his hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are not too far away from the start, but before the action gets underway, there is a moment of tribute for the first responders who showed immense bravery during the recent attacks at Bondi Beach. This is also the Pink Test, dedicated to raising awareness and funds for cancer, particularly breast cancer, in honour of Jane McGrath, the late wife of former cricketer Glenn McGrath, and the work of the McGrath Foundation.

Steve Smith, the captain of Australia, says that they would have batted first as well. Adds that there is a bit of moisture and hopes that the new ball does something. Says that there is a bit of grass, it is soft and the cracks will come into play later on. Mentions that they keep producing pitches that will support pace and seam. Says that it has been a wonderful week. Informs that Beau Webster comes in for Jhye Richardson.

Ben Stokes, the skipper of England, says that the conditions look pretty good for batting, and they want to put up a score on the board. Adds that to get that win in MCG was special and they are looking forward to this one. Informs that Matthew Potts comes in for Gus Atkinson and says that he has been working really hard and is a competitor.

Australia (Playing XI) - Travis Head, Jake Weatherald, Marnus Labuschagne, Steve Smith (C), Usman Khawaja, Alex Carey (WK), Cameron Green, Beau Webster (In place of Jhye Richardson), Michael Neser, Mitchell Starc, Scott Boland.

England (Playing XI) - Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Jacob Bethell, Joe Root, Harry Brook, Ben Stokes (C), Jamie Smith (WK), Will Jacks, Brydon Carse, Josh Tongue, Matthew Potts (In place of Gus Atkinson).
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Ben Stokes and England have elected to BAT first.

England’s chances of a series-ending draw rest heavily on the shoulders of Joe Root and Zak Crawley, who have been the primary pillars of a batting lineup that has otherwise struggled against the Australian bounce. However, they must contend with a wounded Australian side that rarely loses twice in a row at home. With the McGrath Foundation’s sea of pink providing the backdrop, this final encounter is about more than just the trophy; it is a battle for momentum heading into the next cycle of the World Test Championship. Whether England can replicate their Melbourne heroics or Australia sends Khawaja off with a clinical victory remains the defining question of the Sydney New Year. Stay tuned for the toss and sheets.

The Pink Test at the SCG adds its customary layer of emotion and strategy, particularly with the farewell of veteran opener Usman Khawaja, who is set to retire at the conclusion of this match. Historically a surface that offers more for the spinners than other Australian decks, both sides have adjusted their squads accordingly. England has signaled a tactical shift by including off-spinner Shoaib Bashir in their 12-man squad, marking the first time they have opted for a specialist slow bowler this series. Meanwhile, Australia is weighing the inclusion of Todd Murphy to partner their pace attack, which has been spearheaded by the relentless Scott Boland and Mitchell Starc throughout the summer.

Hello and a warm welcome to one and all. The 2025/26 Ashes series reaches its grand finale at the Sydney Cricket Ground with Australia holding an unassailable 3-1 lead. While the Urn is already safely retained by the hosts following dominant victories in Perth, Brisbane, and Adelaide, the narrative shifted dramatically during the Boxing Day Test. England’s stunning four-wicket victory in Melbourne, their first Test win on Australian soil in 15 years, has breathed fresh life into the tour. Led by Steve Smith in the absence of the rested Pat Cummins, Australia will be desperate to re-establish their dominance and finish the summer with a 4-1 scoreline, while Ben Stokes’ men aim to prove that their Bazball defiance can still bridge the gap on the world's toughest touring stage.
